title: Sunday · Cedar
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · from 2017 the aggregator
logline: One of twelve magical-realist Sundays: the smokestack growing back into a tree. Played straight. The phantom novel bleeding through.

panels.composition: Tier 1: the mill in July. The smokestack — but the sapling at its rim is a tree now, a real cedar, twenty feet, its roots down the brick like veins. Played straight.
props: smokestack with a full cedar growing from it

image.prompt: an abandoned mill's brick smokestack with a full cedar tree growing from its top, roots running down the brickwork like veins, July light, rendered completely straight in wet-on-wet watercolor, no people

panels.name: Growing back

panels.composition: Tier 2: inside the shed. The bars of light. And where the saw was, a stump — the floor has become forest floor, sawdust to duff, a fern in the blade slot.
props: a stump where the saw was

image.prompt: the inside of a vast abandoned mill shed where the great saw has become a mossy stump, sawdust turned to forest duff, a fern growing in the blade slot, long bars of light, watercolor

panels.name: The saw

panels.composition: Tier 3: the mill from the road at dusk, the whole shed roofed in moss and saplings, the stack a tree, the chain across the drive still there. The only sign it's a drawing of a wish: the chain.

image.prompt: an abandoned mill seen from the road at dusk transformed into forest, moss and saplings over the shed roof, a cedar on the smokestack, and across the drive still an ordinary rusted chain, watercolor, no words
image.notes: Nothing in the strip says this is imagined. The chain is the tell.

panels.name: The chain

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; the pup's weight learned; Sundays wet-on-wet
art.palette: dailies: ink and one tone. Sundays: gray-green, fog, rust, bruised dusk

notes: Cedar: one of twelve. The mill grows back. The chain stays real.
